name: inspect_scene
description: Inspect committed editor state, including an active manipulation preview (Move, Rotate or Scale), document origin, bounded canonical curve IDs/names/class/counts/domain, retained-source counts and read-only reason, pending human edits and source-appearance readiness. A node's read-only `transform_attributes` (rotate order, rotate axis in degrees, shear, rotate and scale pivots, pivot translations, `inherits_transform`, `offset_parent_matrix` (row-vector as stored, translation row in the scene's linear unit, omitted when it is the identity; the `inherits_transform` false plus offset combination is PROVISIONAL, unverified against Maya) and `non_default`) reports transform extras and is present only when at least one is non-default. Curve draw_available means at least one visible instance prepared as draw geometry; it does not claim GPU health or framebuffer success. `status_message` mirrors the native status line text (null when empty, capped at 512 characters, a fixed notice instead of file-error text that can carry a local path). `camera` reports the pose: target, eye, distance, yaw/pitch in degrees, vertical field of view at the current viewport aspect and clip planes. `manipulation.viewport` reports the last native pointer's pick: `pointer_hit` for the active tool's handle and `pointer_disabled` for a drawn-but-unsupported handle and `pointer_refusal` for why a Rotate or Scale press there would be refused (with a hit: that handle; with a null hit: the whole tool, for example a mirrored frame; null for Move), all null during an active manipulation. They mirror the painted highlight, so window focus, an open popup or a file modal do not null them; a hidden window has no `viewport`, and a view build error (for example an overflowing scale) nulls `viewport` from the first frame after the edit until a frame builds a view. No CV arrays or script bodies are exposed. A scene too large for one reply is read in pages: pass `node_limit` (50 to 100 suits most clients) and follow `page.next_cursor` while `page.truncated` is true; the cursor goes stale (`stale_scene`) as soon as the scene changes, and then the walk restarts without a cursor. Every page repeats the selection, camera and editor state; a shape or curve appears on the page of the node that holds it

cursor.description:
The `page.next_cursor` of the previous paged reply; requires `node_limit`. It is opaque
and valid only until the scene changes.

node_limit.description:
Return at most this many nodes (1 to 4096), with the shapes and curves they hold. Omit it
for one reply with the whole scene.

name: set_active_tool
description: Select the native Select, Move, Rotate or Scale tool; unsupported tools are not exposed

name: set_tool_space
description: Set the Axis Orientation of the Move or Scale (object, world or parent) or Rotate (object or world) tool settings, the same setting as the native Tool Settings selector; read it from inspect_scene manipulation.move_space, rotate_space and scale_space. A move begun with begin_manipulation uses the Move setting, so each selected object moves along its own orientation axes; a scale begun with begin_manipulation names its own space, and the native Scale drag refuses the Parent setting until its handles follow it. Does not change the active tool

MoveSpaceInput.description: The Move tool also works in its parent's axes (`parent`).

ScaleSpaceInput.description: Scale also works in its parent's axes (`parent`).

SpaceInput.description: Rotate and Scale work in the node's own axes (`object`) or the world axes (`world`).

inputSchema.description:
Sets the Axis Orientation the Move, Rotate or Scale tool settings use for the next
manipulation. Move and Scale accept `parent`; Rotate does not.
inputSchema.title: ToolSpaceArgs

name: set_tool_handle
description: Set the persistent Rotate axis (x, y, z) or Scale handle (x, y, z, uniform) that the native Tool Settings selectors use for numeric entry; read them from inspect_scene manipulation.rotate_axis and scale_handle. begin_manipulation always names its own axis or handle and ignores this setting. Does not change the active tool or space

inputSchema.description:
`tool` selects which persistent selection is set: the Rotate axis or the Scale handle. Each
takes its own field and nothing else.
inputSchema.title: ToolHandleArgs

name: set_manipulator_size
description: Set the global size of the Move, Rotate and Scale manipulators, the same setting as the native + and - keys, from 0.1 to 10.0 (default 1.0); a value set here is rounded to three decimals, so 2.5555 reads back as 2.556. The keys step on the 1.25^k grid (k from -10 to 10, about 0.107 to 9.313) and store the exact grid value, so after a key step inspect_scene may report more decimals (for example 1.5625); a step from an off-grid value moves to the next grid value in that direction that changes the three-decimal value. Session-only: it never dirties the scene or enters undo history. Read it from inspect_scene manipulation.manipulator_size. Below 0.5 the drawn manipulator stops shrinking. Does not change the active tool

inputSchema.description: Sets the global manipulator size. The value is rounded to three decimals.

size.description: Between 0.1 and 10.0 inclusive; 2.5555 is stored and read back as 2.556.

inputSchema.title: ManipulatorSizeArgs

name: begin_manipulation
description: Begin one remote-owned Move (World axis), Rotate (Object or World space) or Scale (Object, World or Parent space) of the exact selected transform instance. Numeric manipulation may begin while any tool is active; this does not change tools. A Move or a Scale acts on the whole current selection with the named node as its lead (the last selected object), each object scaling about its own pivot by the same factor; with several objects selected pass expected_selection_generation from inspect_scene selection_generation, otherwise the call returns multiple_selection, and a value that no longer matches the selection is stale_selection, checked before the target and selection refusals, and changes nothing. Rotate still needs exactly one selected object

ScaleSpaceInput.description: Scale also works in its parent's axes (`parent`).

SpaceInput.description: Rotate and Scale work in the node's own axes (`object`) or the world axes (`world`).

inputSchema.description:
`kind` selects the manipulation; each kind takes its own handle fields and nothing else. Move
works along World axes only and takes no `space`.

expected_selection_generation.description:
The `selection_generation` that `inspect_scene` reported. A Move acts on the whole
current selection with this node as its lead; with several objects selected the value
is required, and a value that no longer matches the selection is refused.

The `selection_generation` that `inspect_scene` reported; the rule is the one of
Move: the Scale acts on the whole current selection with this node as its lead.

inputSchema.title: BeginManipulationArgs

name: update_manipulation
description: Preview an absolute value from begin: distance in the scene linear unit for Move, angle in the scene angular unit for Rotate, a unitless factor greater than zero for Scale. Units are echoed in inspection.manipulation.units. Matching scene token and remote-owned manipulation ID are required; a parameter of the wrong kind is a typed error

inputSchema.description: Exactly one of distance (Move), angle (Rotate) or factor (Scale), matching the kind of the manipulation; any other is a typed manipulation_kind_mismatch error

distance.description: Absolute Move distance from begin along the World axis, in the scene linear unit (inspection units.distance)

angle.description: Absolute Rotate angle from begin about the axis, in the scene angular unit (inspection units.angle)

factor.description: Absolute Scale factor from begin, unitless and greater than zero

inputSchema.title: UpdateManipulationArgs

name: finish_manipulation
description: Commit one undoable Move, Rotate or Scale edit or cancel to the exact begin authoring state. Only the matching remote-owned manipulation ID may finish

name: create_primitive
description: Create a cube, plane, sphere, cylinder, cone or torus in the live editor. Optional options set sizes, subdivisions and axis (x, y or z) for that primitive; omitted fields use the defaults, and fields of other primitives are rejected. Options are validated against a 20,000-face budget per primitive; larger subdivisions are refused with invalid_params

name: select_node
description: Select an object using an optional full transform instance_path; ambiguous objects require a path. Null node_id clears selection without a path

name: modify_selection
description: Add, toggle or remove one object instance in the ordered object selection (Shift, Ctrl and Shift+Ctrl clicks); the last member is the lead. add appends an absent instance as the lead or moves a present one to the end, toggle flips membership, remove drops a member and leaves an absent one unchanged; removing the lead promotes the previous member. Ambiguous objects require a full instance_path; Object and Hierarchy modes only. Not idempotent; does not edit the scene

name: select_by_rule
description: Select > All, Hierarchy or Inverse by rule. all selects every transform instance, nested ones included, with the last as the lead (only the roots in Hierarchy selection mode); hierarchy adds every descendant of the selected objects and keeps the lead (no change in Hierarchy selection mode); inverse selects the unselected instances (roots only in Hierarchy selection mode; an empty selection selects all). Object and Hierarchy modes only. Not idempotent because inverse flips; does not edit the scene

name: select_in_rect
description: Marquee-select objects by a rectangle in normalised device coordinates (x right, y up, each within -1 to 1; corners in either order), the same typed operation as a viewport drag. mode replace (default, Maya select -replace) sets the selection to the hits, add appends the absent hits, remove (select -deselect) drops the hit members, toggle flips each hit; the hits are in instance order and the last appended or last hit is the lead. Object and Hierarchy modes only (Hierarchy maps hits to their roots). Any overlap of a visible mesh selects it; objects hidden behind others inside the rectangle ARE selected, as in Maya's object marquee (camera-based selection is documented for components only; PROVISIONAL, #30). Hidden instances and curves are not selectable. A zero-area rectangle (min equals max) picks like a click: the nearest hit only. Uses the aspect of the last painted frame (1 before the first), so read the camera with inspect_scene first. A replace with no hit clears the selection; add, remove and toggle with no hit change nothing. Not idempotent because toggle flips; does not edit the scene

NdcRectArgs.description:
A rectangle in normalised device coordinates: x right, y up, both within -1 to 1. The corners
may come in either order.

name: deselect_all
description: Select > Deselect All (Alt+D): clear the object and any face, vertex or edge selection and return to Object selection mode, as Maya's SelectNone does. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene

name: set_selection_mode
description: Set Object, Face, Vertex, Edge or Hierarchy (Root sub-mask only) selection mode without editing the scene; a valid remembered face, vertex or edge stays inactive outside its own mode

name: modify_component_selection
description: Replace, add to, remove from or toggle the face, vertex or edge selection of the one selected object by component index (Maya select -replace, -add, -deselect, -toggle on f[n], vtx[n], e[n]); the same typed operation a component click or drag would use. owner names the selected object's shape as select_face does (node_id, shape_id and the full instance_path ending with the shape); indices are positions in that mesh, so a topology edit or Undo can renumber them, and members past the end are dropped. mode replace (default) sets the set to the indices in order (an empty list empties it), add appends the absent ones, remove drops the members, toggle flips each distinct index; repeated indices keep their first position and the last member is the lead (PROVISIONAL: Maya documents neither order nor lead). Requires the mode of kind (set_selection_mode) and refuses an owner that is not the single selected object without changing the selection, and any index outside the mesh without changing anything. Each type keeps its own set across mode switches; select_face, select_vertex and select_edge still replace the whole set with one component. Read the sets with inspect_scene component_selection. Not idempotent because add, remove and toggle depend on the set; does not edit the scene

ComponentOwnerArgs.description:
The shape instance whose components are selected: the selected object's shape, as
`select_face` names it.

indices.description: Component indices of the owner's mesh; repeats keep their first position.

name: select_face
description: Select a complete canonical face target in Face mode, or clear it with null; explicit targets need not be visible and select their owning instance

name: select_vertex
description: Select a complete canonical vertex target in Vertex mode, or clear it with null; explicit targets need not be visible and select their owning instance

name: select_edge
description: Select a complete canonical edge target in Edge mode, or clear it with null; explicit targets need not be visible and select their owning instance

name: rename_node
description: Rename an existing object

name: set_transform
description: Set f64 translation in declared scene units, rotation in XYZ degrees, and scale

name: edit_node
description: Edit optional name and individual f64 channels in one undo entry. Omitted arrays and null components are untouched; translation uses declared scene units and supplied rotations use degrees. Does not change selection

name: set_pivots
description: Set the rotate and scale pivots of one node in one undo entry named Pivot. Pivots are f64 triples in declared scene units, Object (local) space; World space is unsupported. An omitted pivot is untouched, and both omitted only checks the node and returns unchanged. With preserve true (the default, like xform -preserve; the placement is PROVISIONAL) the node's matrix is kept by compensating through its rotate and scale pivot translates, so the object does not move; with preserve false the raw pivots are written and a rotated or scaled object moves. Does not change selection. On an opened Maya Binary scene a preserve edit is accepted only when no compensation is needed (otherwise pivot_needs_translate_correction), and a node without the rotate or scale pivot record refuses a nonzero value (absent_pivot_leaf, or insertion_after_delete when the scene has removals), and an edit-restricted node refuses with unsupported_edit; Maya ASCII is read-only (read_only_format). A node with session keys refuses (pivot_on_keyed_node). A non-finite input is a protocol error and a value that overflows when applied is invalid_input; nothing changes on any refusal

preserve.description:
Keep the node's matrix by compensating through the rotate and scale pivot translates
(default true, like `xform -preserve`); false writes the raw pivots and the object may move.

rotate_pivot.description: New rotate pivot in declared scene units, Object (local) space. Omit to leave it alone.

scale_pivot.description: New scale pivot in declared scene units, Object (local) space. Omit to leave it alone.

name: reset_pivots
description: Modify > Center Pivot (mode center) or Zero Pivot (mode zero) on every selected object, each handled independently, in one undo entry named Pivot; the object does not move. Center puts both pivots at the centre of the node's hierarchy bounding box in its own Object space, over visible mesh and curve control points (PROVISIONAL); a node with no geometry stays unchanged, and unproved geometry visibility refuses the call with scene_error. Zero puts both pivots at the node's origin and keeps the matrix (PROVISIONAL, follows xform -zeroTransformPivots). Pass expected_selection_generation from inspect_scene; it is required with several objects selected and a mismatch is stale_selection. Object and Hierarchy selection only: component modes return invalid_input and an empty selection returns no_selection. A node with session keys refuses (pivot_on_keyed_node), as do the same Maya Binary and Maya ASCII cases as set_pivots; all or nothing, with the scene and history untouched on any refusal. Component Center Pivot and Bake Pivot are unsupported

expected_selection_generation.description:
The `selection_generation` that `inspect_scene` reported. With several objects selected
the value is required, and a value that no longer matches the selection is refused.

name: extrude_face
description: Extrude one current canonical quad along its local normal by distance in declared scene units. Requires node, shape and full root-to-shape path; shared-shape edits affect every instance. Zero distance changes topology; imported structural edits remain unsupported

name: move_vertices
description: Translate vertices of one polygon mesh together by delta, in declared scene units along the mesh's own axes (the Move tool's Object axis orientation). Requires node, shape and full root-to-shape path and distinct vertex indices; shared-shape edits affect every instance. One undo step. Authored scenes only: scenes opened from a file refuse until their writer can carry edited points. World-axis moves are unsupported

delta.description: Offset along the mesh's own X, Y and Z axes in declared scene units.

name: inspect_vertices
description: Read one shape's vertex positions, up to 1024 per call, as [x, y, z] in declared scene units along the mesh's own axes (f32 precision for single-precision meshes). Reports the scene token and revision of the state read. A large shape is read in pages: follow `next_cursor` until it is null; it goes stale (`stale_scene`) as soon as the scene changes

cursor.description:
The `next_cursor` of the previous reply. It is opaque and valid only until the scene
changes.

name: create_joint
description: Create a session-only joint, the same operation as Skeleton > Create Joints: a bare transform that stays selected, with rotation 0 and scale 1. `parent_id` must name a joint and is the only way to attach it; the selection is not read. A world `position` under a parent is solved through the parent's world matrix and refused when that matrix is singular; `relative` stores the position as given. A joint under a joint keeps segment scale compensation on. A scene holding joints cannot be saved, and joints are not written to any file. Refused on an opened scene, in a component selection mode, for a parent that is not a joint, a radius of 0 or less or above 1000000, an invalid or colliding name and past the hierarchy depth limit. `inspect_scene` reports `joint.radius` on each joint; `delete_node` removes a joint with everything below it, as one undo step

name.description: Omit it for the lowest free `joint<N>`.

parent_id.description: The joint to parent under; omit it to start a new hierarchy. The selection is not read.

position.description: World position, or the offset from the parent when `relative` is true. Default the origin.

radius.description: Greater than 0 and at most 1000000. Default 1.

relative.description: Measure `position` from the parent. Without a parent it changes nothing. Default false.

name: set_current_time
description: Move the current time to a whole frame and write every keyed channel's value there. This is not an undo step and does not dirty a scene with no keys. Fractional times are refused with invalid_frame. A human draft refuses it with busy_editing, and a manipulation with busy_manipulation. A manual edit of a keyed channel holds until the next time change, then snaps back to the keys (PROVISIONAL). Stops playback

name: set_keyframe
description: Key transform channels with their current value, as one undo step. No time means the current time, no node_ids means the object selection (Object or Hierarchy mode), and no channels means all nine transform channels. Keys are session-only whole-frame values, interpolated linearly and held outside them (PROVISIONAL: tangents are not implemented). Rotation values are in the scene's declared angular unit. Sourced scenes refuse keys, and a scene holding keys cannot be saved. Bounded by key_limit. Stops playback

channels.description: Omit it for all nine transform channels.

node_ids.description: The objects to act on. Omit it for the object selection.

name: delete_keys
description: Delete keys as one undo step: at `time`, or at every frame when it is omitted. No node_ids means the object selection, and no channels means all nine. Remaining keys are evaluated at the current time; a channel left with no key keeps its pose. Stops playback

channels.description: Omit it for all nine transform channels.

node_ids.description: The objects to act on. Omit it for the object selection.

name: set_playback_range
description: Set the playback range in whole frames. Session-only, not an undo step. The start must not be after the end (invalid_playback_range). Stops playback

name: play_timeline
description: Start playback at 24 fps, looping continuously over the playback range, skipping frames rather than slowing down (rate and loop PROVISIONAL). A time outside the range starts at the range start. It advances only while the native window renders. It stops on a manipulation, a focused text field, a draft, a file modal or close. A request that passes the scene token and busy checks stops it before it runs, even when a later check refuses the request; a request refused by those checks, such as a stale scene_token, leaves it playing. The exceptions are requests that only select (objects, by rule or components, or the selection mode), set the active tool, its space or handle or the manipulator size, frame the view, orbit, pan, dolly or set the camera pose, set the grid, the shading mode, a sidebar panel or the Attribute Editor tab, or read with inspect_scene, inspect_keys or inspect_uvs, and play_timeline, which leaves playback running (a repeated call is unchanged), and stop_timeline, which stops it itself. Read `timeline.playing`. Each frame that moves a keyed channel changes the revision, so paged cursors go stale during playback

name: stop_timeline
description: Stop playback, leaving the current time where it is

name: inspect_keys
description: Read stored keys in node, channel and frame order, optionally for one object. On a sourced scene `unavailable_reason` says source animation curves are not exposed or evaluated, which does not mean there are none. A large table is read in pages: follow `next_cursor` until it is null; it goes stale (`stale_scene`) as soon as the scene changes, including on playback ticks

cursor.description:
The `next_cursor` of the previous reply, for the same `node_id`. It is opaque and valid
only until the scene changes.

name: project_uv_planar
description: Replace a shape's map1 with a planar projection from the object-space X, Y or Z axis, fitted to the object-space bounds of the face corners so u and v fill 0 through 1. The axis-to-(u, v) assignment, oriented as the side, top and front views (view-matching, right-handed), and the Y default are PROVISIONAL. Authored shapes only. UVs are saved to an authored Maya ASCII .ma and reopen from it (the .mb writer refuses them with save_unwritable reason session_uvs: Delete UVs or Undo to save a .mb). Extrude is refused on a shape with UVs. A shape with no extent across the projection is refused with degenerate_uv_projection

axis.description: Project from this object-space axis. Omit it for Y (PROVISIONAL).

name: delete_uvs
description: Remove a shape's map1. A shape without UVs returns unchanged

name: inspect_uvs
description: Read one shape's map1 (session-only until saved to an authored .ma, which reopens with it): one [u, v] per outer corner of each face, in face order, in single precision (f32 values). `uv_set` is null when the shape has no UVs. On a sourced scene `unavailable_reason` says source UVs are not exposed, which does not mean the shape has none. A large set is read in pages: follow `next_cursor` until it is null; it goes stale (`stale_scene`) as soon as the scene changes

cursor.description:
The `next_cursor` of the previous reply. It is opaque and valid only until the scene
changes.

name: set_material_diffuse
description: Edit the checked saved Phong diffuse scalar for an exact shape through shared undo history. Requires complete shared-shader users; affects all those shapes. Values are finite and nonnegative, may exceed one, and do not enable rendered materials

name: create_session_material
description: Create a session-only lambert material (not saved: while one exists, a scene that can otherwise save refuses Save and Save As with save_unwritable (save_ascii_write for .ma) until it is undone; a scene with a retained source, such as an opened Maya file, refuses, while new and legacy JSON scenes accept) with a linear RGB colour (stored in single precision: each channel is rounded to the nearest f32), as its own undo step. Replies with its material_id. Material ids are decimal table indices valid only at the current history position: undo or redo can free and reuse them, so never cache one across edits

name: assign_session_material
description: Assign a session material to a whole authored shape; every instance of the shape changes. Give material_id (existing) or color (creates a lambert in the same undo step). Replies with the material_id, or unchanged. Not saved: while a session material exists, a scene that can otherwise save refuses Save and Save As with save_unwritable (save_ascii_write for .ma) until it is undone. A scene with a retained source, such as an opened Maya file, refuses; new and legacy JSON scenes accept. Material ids are decimal table indices valid only at the current history position: undo or redo can free and reuse them, so never cache one across edits

color.description: Creates a new lambert with this colour in the same undo step. Give this or `material_id`.

material_id.description: An existing material id from inspection or a create reply. Give this or `color`.

name: set_session_material_color
description: Set the linear RGB colour of a session material created in this session (stored in single precision: each channel is rounded to the nearest f32); the initial material 0 is locked. Not saved; unrelated to the saved Phong set_material_diffuse. Material ids are decimal table indices valid only at the current history position: undo or redo can free and reuse them, so never cache one across edits

name: delete_node
description: Delete an object and all its descendants through editor undo history; the form of Maya's delete command with no flags, applied to one node (PROVISIONAL: the documentation does not state the default of -hierarchy, so the subtree semantics are pinned by tests). A descendant transform that also hangs under a node outside the subtree is refused; a shape shared with such a node stays. Refused in Face, Vertex or Edge selection mode

name: delete_selected
description: Delete every selected object (Edit > Delete) as one undo step; the form of Maya's delete command with no flags, each node removed with its whole subtree (PROVISIONAL, see delete_node; that the Edit > Delete menu item runs exactly this form, not a wrapper script, is also PROVISIONAL). All or nothing: if any selected object or its subtree cannot be deleted (a shared descendant, or an opened file whose records cannot be dropped) the whole delete is refused with that object's error and nothing changes. A selected descendant of another selected object is deleted once, with it. The selection is empty afterwards and Undo restores the objects but not the selection. Refused in Face, Vertex or Edge selection mode and with nothing selected

name: undo
description: Undo the last editor authoring operation

name: redo
description: Redo the last undone authoring operation

name: set_undo_queue
description: Set the Undo queue (Preferences > Undo): finite with a size from 1 to 1000 (default finite 50) or infinite. A smaller size drops the oldest steps at once. Session-only: it survives New and Open but not a restart. Refused while an undo chunk or manipulation is open. Read it from inspect_scene undo_state

size.description: Finite queue size, 1 to 1000; required for "finite", refused for "infinite".

name: set_undo_enabled
description: Turn Undo on or off (undoInfo -state, or -stateWithoutFlush with flush false). While off, edits apply and record nothing, Undo and Redo do nothing, and an edit flushes both queues so no stale step can erase it. Refused while an undo chunk or manipulation is open. Read it from inspect_scene undo_state

flush.description: Clear both queues (`undoInfo -state`) or keep them (`-stateWithoutFlush`). Default true when turning undo off and false when turning it on (PROVISIONAL: the docs state no flush rule).

name: open_undo_chunk
description: Start an undo chunk: every edit until close_undo_chunk joins one undo step named name (default Chunk). Chunks do not nest. While one is open the native Undo and Redo close it first, so an abandoned chunk cannot block them; an open chunk is reported by inspect_scene undo_state.open_chunk. Close every chunk you open: until then edits from any source, native ones included, join it

name.description: Name of the single undo step, at most 64 characters; empty or omitted is "Chunk".

name: close_undo_chunk
description: Close the open undo chunk and record its edits as one undo step; a chunk with no net scene change records no step

name: frame_selected
description: Frame the selected objects using the live camera (Maya F): the union of the selected objects' own geometry (meshes, curves and joints) without their descendants, or with them when with_children is true (Ctrl+F; default false). A selection where no object owns visible geometry frames the objects' origins when with_children is false; with_children true on such a selection is refused and the camera is unchanged. In face, vertex and edge modes it frames the selected face corners, the remembered vertex or both endpoints of the remembered edge and ignores with_children. Nothing selected in object or hierarchy mode frames everything like frame_all (an empty scene returns nothing_to_frame); in the component modes it returns no_selection. Optional fit_factor (Maya viewFit -fitFactor) is the fraction of the view (limiting axis) the framed geometry fills, from 0.01 to 1 (the default margin is about 0.95); a value outside that range returns invalid_input and keeps the camera

fit_factor.description:
Maya viewFit -fitFactor: the fraction of the view (limiting axis) the framed objects fill,
from 0.01 to 1 (PROVISIONAL range). Omit for the default framing margin.

with_children.description: Also frame the selected objects' descendants (Maya Ctrl+F). Default false (Maya F).

name: frame_all
description: Frame every mesh, curve and joint in the scene using the live camera; a scene with none of these returns nothing_to_frame. Optional fit_factor (Maya viewFit -fitFactor): the fraction of the view (limiting axis) the framed objects fill, from 0.01 to 1; omit for the default margin (about 0.95); a value outside that range returns invalid_input and keeps the camera. Session-only; does not edit the scene or the selection

fit_factor.description:
Maya viewFit -fitFactor: the fraction of the view (limiting axis) the framed objects fill,
from 0.01 to 1 (PROVISIONAL range). Omit for the default framing margin.

name: set_grid_visibility
description: Set the current viewport's grid visibility explicitly. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene or report GPU health

name: set_shading_mode
description: Set the current viewport's shading mode explicitly to wireframe or smooth_shade_all. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene, change picking or report GPU health

ShadingMode.description: Session-only viewport shading, like grid visibility; never saved or dirtying.

name: orbit_camera
description: Orbit the live camera by [yaw, pitch] radians; pitch clamps near the poles

name: set_camera_pose
description: Set the live camera to an absolute pose: target [x, y, z], distance, yaw_degrees and pitch_degrees, the values inspect_scene reports, so a read pose restores exactly. Yaw wraps; pitch beyond about ±89.94 degrees is rejected. The field of view and clip planes are untouched; a distance below near_clip puts the target closer to the eye than the near plane (between the eye and the plane), so it is clipped and not pickable. Session-only; does not edit the scene

name: pan_camera
description: Translate the live camera target by [right, up] camera-plane world units

name: dolly_camera
description: Multiply live camera distance by a positive finite factor; below one moves closer

name: set_snap_mode
description: Set Snap to grids explicitly (Status Line button, `snapMode -grid`); off by default. While on, a Move begun with begin_manipulation lands the lead object's pivot on the nearest line of the drawn grid (one line per centimetre) along its axis, absolute rather than relative; the rest of the selection moves by the same distance. The Move axis must lie along a world X, Y or Z axis (World orientation, or Object or Parent aligned to the world): otherwise begin_manipulation returns invalid_input and nothing starts. A pivot within a few ulps of a line stays put. Only grid snapping exists: curve, point, surface and relative step snapping are not implemented. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene. Refused with busy_manipulation during any manipulation and busy_editing during a modal or close; inspect_scene snap_to_grid reports the state

grid.description: Snap to grids on or off.

name: set_menu_set
description: Switch the menu set the native menu bar shows, like the Status Line selector or F2 and F3. Only modeling and rigging exist; Animation, FX and Rendering are not implemented. Session-only and idempotent: it does not edit the scene, mark it dirty or change the scene token, New and Open keep it, and it cannot be undone. Refused while a file dialog is open. `inspect_scene` reports it as `menu_set`

name: set_sidebar_panel_visibility
description: Set one sidebar panel's visibility explicitly. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene. The dock shows one panel: showing attribute_editor hides channel_box and the reverse

name: select_attribute_editor_tab
description: Select the Attribute Editor tab for the selected node: transform, a direct shape, or the material of a direct shape; only the first 16 direct shapes have tabs. Session-only and idempotent; does not edit the scene. Refused unless attribute_editor is the active sidebar panel, and refused when the tab does not resolve for the current selection or names a shape beyond the 16th

id.description: Decimal id: the selected node for `transform`, a direct shape for `shape` and `material`.

name: open_scene
description: Open a Maya binary .mb, supported read-only static curve Maya ASCII .ma, or legacy .aztec scene from a local UTF-8 path (1 to 4096 bytes, no NUL). ASCII scripts stay inert; unsupported commands/effects refuse the whole candidate. Dirty documents require confirmation. Imported ASCII scenes remain read-only; a mesh .ma written unchanged by this editor's ASCII Save opens on macOS and Linux as an editable, saveable authored document, and any other mesh .ma is refused

name: save_scene
description: Save the active supported Maya binary document, or on Unix an authored Maya ASCII document previously saved by this editor, or reconcile an earlier uncertain installation without another write. On Unix, a new Untitled scene returns save_needs_path: use save_scene_as for a fresh .mb or .ma. Imported ASCII scenes remain read-only. Untitled saves are unsupported on Windows. PROVISIONAL: Maya acceptance of new-scene files is unproven; an authored .ma carries each shape's session map1 UVs (the .mb writer does not and refuses them: use Delete UVs or Undo to save a .mb), and the UV layout in the file is unchecked against Maya

name: save_scene_as
description: Save a supported Maya binary scene to a fresh .mb path without overwriting. On Unix only, a new Untitled scene, or an authored document previously saved by this editor as either .ma or .mb, can be written as a Maya 2025-format .mb or as Maya ASCII .ma, chosen by the extension; an opened Maya binary scene refuses .ma with save_ascii_write. Unsupported content is refused (save_unwritable for .mb, with a stable error.reason such as session_materials or session_uvs, save_ascii_write for .ma, for example any session material, created or assigned: undo it to save; session UVs are not a .ma refusal). An uncertain prior save is reconciled instead. PROVISIONAL: Maya acceptance of new-scene files is unproven, an authored .ma carries each shape's session map1 UVs and reopens with them as an authored document (the UV layout in the file is unchecked against Maya), and a scene with UVs is refused as .mb with save_unwritable reason session_uvs

name: export_obj
description: Export displayed polygon geometry as a new Wavefront OBJ file (File > Export All, or Export Selection with selection_only), the same operation as the native menu. World-space f64 positions in centimeters, one object per instance, faces only: no normals, UVs, groups or materials. Never overwrites; the scene is not changed. Replies with object, vertex and face counts

path.description: New .obj destination; an existing file is never replaced.

selection_only.description:
Export only every selected object and its descendants (Export Selection); default false
exports every displayed polygon instance (Export All).

name: import_obj
description: Import a Wavefront OBJ file into the current scene (File > Import), the same operation as the native menu. Adds one new root object per o/g group (faces before any group take the file name) as one undo step, selects them, and keeps the scene token. Meshes only: v and f records (triangles, quads, n-gons, negative indices); normals, UVs, materials, smoothing and .mtl are counted in ignored_records and dropped. Refuses free-form geometry, unknown records, overlapping groups, CR-only line endings and faces the viewport cannot display (concave or holed faces with 5 or more corners: triangulate and export again). Refused in a scene opened from .mb or .ma. PROVISIONAL: Maya's help is silent on units, naming, winding and limits. Replies with object, vertex and face counts and the new node_ids

path.description: Existing .obj file to add to the scene.

name: new_scene
description: Request a new empty document; dirty documents require explicit confirmation using the returned pending_action_id

name: resolve_file_action
description: Cancel, discard, save or save_as (with a fresh path; the only save for a pending Untitled scene) before the exact pending file action using its UUID and current scene token; a failed save leaves the prompt pending; source-changed Open requires Cancel and reopening

path.description: Fresh destination, required for and only allowed with decision save_as (1 to 4096 bytes).

name: request_close
description: Request native window closure; dirty documents require explicit confirmation, and approved remote closure waits for its successful reply to be flushed
